rot.imbalances.ideia.sveshnikov.e1: Attack: from White's side, in the Sicilian, Sveshnikov Variation. No check, capture or threat wins material. In a quiet position like this, the plan comes from the differences between the sides: the imbalances.
rot.imbalances.ideia.sveshnikov.e2: White's imbalances: the knight on d5 stands on an outpost, and the black pawn on d6 is backward, on the d-file, which is half-open for White.
rot.imbalances.ideia.sveshnikov.e3: Black's imbalance: Black has the bishop pair, on c8 and g5, against one bishop and two knights. With the list of both sides, each one knows what to play for.
rot.imbalances.ideia.sveshnikov.l1: The bishop goes to c4 and defends the knight on d5. White reinforces the outpost, White's imbalance, and the knight stays firm in the centre.
rot.imbalances.ideia.sveshnikov.l2: Defence: the rook goes to b8, on the b-file, half-open for Black, and attacks the pawn on b2. Black also plays for an imbalance of its own.
rot.imbalances.ideia.sveshnikov.l3: In quiet positions like this, each side chooses an imbalance in its favour and plays for it. The order is this: first, check the checks, captures and threats; with no tactic, play by the list.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.p: Find the move that uses the outpost knight to win material.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.certo: The knight leaves f4 with check, and the queen attacks the bishop on e3.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.revela: The knight on f4 goes to h3 and gives check. As it leaves, it opens the diagonal of the queen on g5 to the bishop on e3, which nobody defends.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.err.g7g6.1: The pawn goes to g6 and blocks the diagonal of the bishop on h7, but your knight still stands in the middle of the queen's diagonal.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.err.g7g6.2: The bishop on e3 captures the knight on f4, and the position is equal.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.err.g7g6.3: Back to the position: the knight can leave f4 with check.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.err.g5h6.1: The queen leaves g5 and gives up the diagonal to the bishop on e3.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.err.g5h6.2: The bishop on h7 comes back to e4, and White loses no material.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.err.g5h6.3: Back to the position: leave the queen on g5 and play the knight.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.fora: That move does not use the knight or the queen. Play one of those pieces.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.volta: Try again: look for the knight move with check.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.e1: Attack: now from Black's side, in the game DHC vs CopiniMonster, Lichess 2020. Here there are checks, and the list shows where to look: the knight on f4 stands on an outpost, defended by the pawn on e5.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.e2: No white pawn can drive this knight away. It stands in the middle of the diagonal between your queen on g5 and the bishop on e3, which no white piece defends.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.l0: White must answer the check before saving the bishop.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.l1: Defence: the king gets out of check and goes to g2. White has no time to save the bishop.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.l2: The queen captures the bishop on e3, and Black wins a piece.
rot.imbalances.ideia.posto.l3: The tactic was born from the imbalance: the outpost knight, the strong piece on the list, gave the check that won the bishop. In positions like this, the list shows the piece, and calculation confirms the move.
rot.imbalances.demos.passados.1: Attack demonstration: still with Black, in the game Pudex vs ozgurgumus, Lichess 2020. The pawns on d3 and e3 are passed and connected: they advance side by side, and one defends the other.
rot.imbalances.demos.passados.2: In the list, White has the rooks on the f-file, but the passed pawns deep in White's camp weigh more. Black's plan is the bigger imbalance: advance them both.
rot.imbalances.demos.passados.l.3: The pawn goes to d2 and threatens to queen on d1. The white king cannot capture it: the pawn on e3 defends it.
rot.imbalances.demos.passados.l.4: Defence: the king goes to c2 and watches d1, the queening square of the pawn on d2.
rot.imbalances.demos.passados.l.5: The pawn on e3 goes to e2 and attacks the rook on f1. Now there are two pawns on the second rank, and White cannot stop both.
rot.imbalances.demos.passados.l.6: In positions like this, connected passed pawns advance together. With them on the list, the plan is to push them, and the pieces only clear the way.
rot.imbalances.demos.coluna.1: Attack demonstration: again with White, in the game AvtomatKalashnikova vs Sevan-94, Lichess 2017. The two white rooks are doubled on the f-file, which is open: no pawn closes it.
rot.imbalances.demos.coluna.2: In the list, this is White's imbalance. The passed pawn on e6 defends f7, on the seventh rank, next to the black king and the knight on e7.
rot.imbalances.demos.coluna.l.3: The rook goes to f7 with check, defended by the pawn on e6. On the seventh rank, it attacks the king and the knight on e7 at the same time.
rot.imbalances.demos.coluna.l.4: Defence: the king escapes to g8. If the rook on f8 captured on f7, the other white rook would recapture with check and also win the knight.
rot.imbalances.demos.coluna.l.5: The rook captures the knight on e7, and White wins a piece.
rot.imbalances.demos.coluna.l.6: In positions like this, the open file is the rooks' road to the seventh rank. The check was born from that imbalance: the list showed the file, and calculation found the move.
rot.imbalances.demos.excecao.1: Attack demonstration: still with White, now the exception, in the game tmaltz vs kumbitmaka, Lichess 2019. In the list, the imbalance is Black's: the bishop pair and an extra piece.
rot.imbalances.demos.excecao.2: But the black king, on h7, has few squares: the knight on e7 controls g8 and g6, and the pawn on g5 controls h6. With checks in the position, calculation comes before the list.
rot.imbalances.demos.excecao.l.3: The rook goes to f7 and gives check along the seventh rank.
rot.imbalances.demos.excecao.l.4: Defence: the bishop blocks the check on g7. The king had no good square: on h8, the other rook would give mate along the h-file.
rot.imbalances.demos.excecao.l.5: The rook goes to h2 and gives mate along the h-file. The bishop on g7, pinned by the rook on f7, cannot block the check.
rot.imbalances.demos.excecao.l.6: Here, the list favoured Black, but White's check came first. Check the checks, captures and threats first: if there is a tactic, it decides, even against the list.
rot.imbalances.pratica.passado.enunciado: Game pitopi vs Chesspirate_Channel, Lichess 2020. No check or capture wins material: the position is quiet. Make the list and play for the imbalance in your favour. Play as Black.
rot.imbalances.pratica.passado.fim: The passed pawn on b5 advanced two squares and reached b3, defended by your queen on c4. With no tactic in the position, the plan came from the list: the passed pawn was your imbalance.
rot.imbalances.pratica.bispos.enunciado: Game harrycane vs MR-Incognito, Lichess 2020. Black has the queen, but you have the bishop pair and the position is open. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.imbalances.pratica.bispos.fim: The list showed the bishop pair, and calculation found the check: the bishop on b2 captured on f6 along the long diagonal, and attacked the rook on d8 at the same time. In an open position, the bishops reach both ends of the board.
rot.imbalances.pratica.bispos.err.e6e7: 30.Re7+? gives check, but after 30...Kh6 the king leaves the diagonal, and Black is better.
rot.imbalances.pratica.bispos.err.e6f6: 30.Rxf6? captures the pawn, but occupies f6, the square of the check by the bishop on b2: after 30...Rxd5 31.cxd5, Black, with the queen, has a decisive advantage.
rot.imbalances.pratica.valeAqui.enunciad: Game ziiver vs chesslanderr, Lichess 2020. In the list, White has the bishop pair and a passed pawn on e5. Is it worth playing by the list here? Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.imbalances.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The queen captured the bishop on g3 with check and, after the pawn recaptured, the rook gave mate on h1. With a tactic in the position, White's list did not count.
rot.imbalances.pratica.valeAqui.err.e3f1: 43...Nf1? threatens the bishop on g3, but after 44.Qxf5+, White has a decisive advantage.
rot.imbalances.pratica.valeAqui.err.e3g4: 43...Ng4? attacks the pawn on e5, but after 44.Qxf5+, White has a decisive advantage.
rot.imbalances.pratica.valeAqui.err.g1g3: 43...Rxg3+? captures the bishop with the rook, but after 44.hxg3, White has a decisive advantage.
rot.imbalances.pratica.valeAqui.err.g7h6: 43...Qh6? retreats the queen, but after 44.Qe7+, White has a decisive advantage.
